one_month_reasoning: The window contains Q3 2026 results (expected ~Oct 22, 2026; consensus EPS ~$0.77 per a secondary source), which will show H2 volumes (management guided H2 copper sales >20% above H1, gold >65% higher) and first detail on the 2027 outlook, plus any Indonesia IUPK extension decision management said it expected 'this year' and any US Section 232 refined-copper tariff news (the Sept 8 White House deadline passed with no decision, and COMEX fell 4.7% on Sept 10). FCX has beaten the last quarter ($0.74 vs $0.59) but fell on the print, so I take no directional earnings view. Copper is near a record with a tariff premium that could unwind, which is a mild downside skew, offset by momentum. Net: an essentially symmetric lognormal around $70.58 at ~13.7% monthly vol (48%/3.5), with a small drag so P(>=spot) is 0.475.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E on my 2027 EPS (~$4.10 at $6.00/lb copper, built from management's 2027 EBITDA sensitivity of $13B at $5 to $20B at $7) x 17x = $70, an FCF-yield value of $69 and a mid-cycle P/E check of $66. Weighted 50/30/20 this gives ~$69, close to the $70.58 spot.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2027E EPS $4.10 x 17x. EPS = (EBITDA $16.9B at $6.00 Cu - D&A ~$2.5B - interest ~$0.4B) x (1-32% tax) x (1-38% NCI share) / 1.44B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: COMEX was at a $6.83 record on Sept 22 and FCX realized $6.17 in Q2. Goldman puts LME fair value at $11,500/t (~$5.22/lb) with ~$2,800/t of tariff premium in the price. I assume partial mean reversion to $6.00.
$13B + (6.00-5.00) x $3.9B per $1/lb, from management's modeled range
H1 2026 effective rate was 30% (37% in H1 2025); I use 32%, weighted toward Indonesia as Grasberg ramps

inputs_detail.input: Noncontrolling interest share of net income
inputs_detail.derivation: H1 2026 NCI took $913M of $2,778M (33%); FCX owns 48.76% of PT-FI and 55.66% of Cerro Verde, so the NCI share rises as Grasberg returns
Consensus 2027 EPS ~$3.95-4.14 against a ~$72 consensus target implies ~17-18x. Volume growth into 2028 supports a mid-to-high teens multiple, trimmed for peak-price earnings.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 OCF $12.5B at $6 Cu - capex $4.8B = $7.7B; x 65% attributable = $5.0B = $3.47/sh; at a 5% yield = $69

inputs_detail.derivation: Interpolated from management's $9.5B at $5 to $15.5B at $7
Roughly 1 minus the NCI share (PT-FI 48.76% and Cerro Verde 55.66% owned)
Consistent with the consensus target and EPS framework, and typical for a large-cap copper producer at elevated prices
A higher multiple on normalized (non-peak) earnings, near the low end of the consensus EPS range

bear.story: The tariff premium unwinds, the US stockpile of ~1.1Mt is released and demand slows, taking copper to ~$4.75-5.00/lb. A Grasberg ramp setback (wet ore, block-cave downtime) or a delayed IUPK extension adds to it. 2027 EPS ~$2.8 at 16x.

base.story: Grasberg reaches ~80% by mid-2027, copper sales rise >20% in 2027, copper averages ~$5.75-6.25 and the IUPK extension is granted. The market pays ~16-17x for 2028 volume growth of ~$4.2-4.5 EPS.

bull.story: Mine disasters keep supply short and copper holds above $7/lb (EBITDA >$20B). A US 232 tariff lifts COMEX-priced US sales, the leach push toward 800Mlb is validated and Bagdad goes ahead. EPS ~$5.5 x 18x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$46 (~35% down) the stock would be discounting copper sustainably under ~$5/lb or a failure of the Grasberg recovery or the IUPK extension (ownership already steps down to ~37% from 2042). That would be a fundamental break of the volume-plus-price thesis, not ordinary 48%-vol noise.

Execution and safety of the Grasberg Block Cave ramp after the 2025 mud rush

reasoning: Primary documents give the operating frame. Q2 2026 beat ($0.74 adj EPS vs $0.59) with a realized price of $6.17/lb. 2026 guidance is 3.1B lb copper, 650k oz gold, $1.90/lb unit costs, $4.3B capex, net debt $2.1B ex smelter debt and 1.44B shares. Management's 2027 model has copper sales +20%, gold +50%, capex $4.8B and EBITDA of $13B at $5 to $20B at $7 copper. The 10-Q adds that NCI took 33% of H1 net income, that ownership drops to ~37% after 2041 under the extension, and that restoration costs were $1.2B for 2026. Converting the EBITDA range to attributable EPS gives ~$4.10 at $6 copper, in line with a consensus 2027 EPS of ~$4.0 and a consensus target of ~$72. Fair value across P/E, FCF yield and mid-cycle methods is ~$69, roughly the spot price, so I see no valuation edge. The stock prices a copper deck near today's record less some tariff premium. Distribution: median ~$71, lognormal with sigma ~0.42 (a little below the 48% realized vol, since the Grasberg-restart event vol is fading), with the left tail slightly fattened for a tariff-premium unwind or a reversal of the copper spike. Scenarios $45/$72/$100 at 25/50/25 give a mean of ~$72.
